# Current implementation contracts and acceptance

This is the current specification for the new federation release. Each contract and criterion appears once with its canonical IDs. All are planned obligations, not passing implementation results. C0/A1/B1/H1/M1/M2/S1 name exact hashes captured in each fixture manifest.

## 1. autonomous local execution

FR-MCP-174 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001 / TEST-MCP-222. Phase: Ph2. Workflows: U02, U03, U06.

Every node, including the hub, performs authorized local business operations and persists results without hub connectivity.

Local request routing binds immutable ProjectId, NodeId and Branch to one DbContext and branch write gate. Dolt-mode domain requests never invoke LocalProxy forwarding or wait for the hub. Existing local authentication remains mandatory; federation reference-token introspection is not a dependency of local work. Result fields distinguish local persistence, version commit and publication.

- **NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable** (`ac-NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable`): Given A/main=C0 and the hub link is down, when A changes TODO T1.title from old to local, then the local API succeeds, a local reread returns local, and no hub request or history commit occurs.
- **HubUsesSameLocalExecution** (`ac-HubUsesSameLocalExecution`): Given H/main=C0 and the gateway is stopped, when H edits T1.title, then H persists it locally while remote/main remains C0.
- **OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite** (`ac-OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite`): Given the prior offline edit, when the application and Dolt restart, then T1.title remains local and main remains C0 until an explicit version commit.

## 2. explicit version commits and publication boundary

FR-MCP-175 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-002 / TEST-MCP-223. Phase: Ph4. Workflows: U02, U07, U09.

Only an explicit version-history commit triggers publication; drafts and SQL saves remain local. Commit retries recover the same history identity.

POST /qbrainai/federation/projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits accepts requestId UUID, expectedHead, expectedWorkingSet, leaseFence, author and message. Success is 201 with commitHash and publicationState=committed_locally. Persist requestId in the Dolt commit trailer. Retry returns the original hash. Head/fingerprint/fence mismatch is HTTP409 with head_changed/working_set_changed/lease_lost. SaveChanges and control.poll never create version commits.

- **SaveDoesNotPublish** (`ac-SaveDoesNotPublish`): Given main=C0 and remote=C0, when SaveChanges persists T1.title=draft, then main and remote stay C0 and no publication intent is emitted.
- **VersionCommitTriggersSync** (`ac-VersionCommitTriggersSync`): Given that draft and a valid preview, when commit request R1 succeeds, then main=A1, the reply says committed_locally, and one recoverable publication intent targets A1.
- **HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft** (`ac-HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft`): Given B has a draft and desired head A1, when B polls, then outcome=waiting_local_work, B/main=C0 and the draft value is unchanged.
- **OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart** (`ac-OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart`): Given A1 committed while disconnected and a crash before intent persistence, when A restarts, then history scanning rediscovers A1 exactly once and publishes it after reconnect.

## 3. logical project enrollment and initial clone

FR-MCP-176 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-003 / TEST-MCP-224. Phase: Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01.

Nodes enroll a logical project under immutable shared identity while retaining host-local paths and refusing destructive clones.

Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.

ProjectEnrollment stores ProjectId UUID, NodeId, ownerSubjectId, normalized local path, schemaVersion and subscriptions. POST /qbrainai/federation/enroll accepts an authenticated pre-provisioned node client plus operator-authorized owner binding. Body ProjectId must be allowed by token scope fed.project.{ProjectId}.enroll and durable membership. Paths stay host-local; no default-workspace fallback. A nonempty clone destination returns409 target_not_empty.

Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.

- **DifferentHostPathsSameProject** (`ac-DifferentHostPathsSameProject`): Given LAB path /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer and LEGION path F:/github/McpServer, when both enroll as ProjectId Atlas, then both reference Atlas and retain their distinct local paths.
- **CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget** (`ac-CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget`): Given target has TODO X, when clone is requested, then409 target_not_empty leaves X and all target files unchanged.
- **UnauthorizedProjectDenied** (`ac-UnauthorizedProjectDenied`): Given node A has only Atlas membership, when it enrolls or clones SecretProject, then403 unauthorized_project returns no rows, objects or project existence details.
- **PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics** (`ac-PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics`): Given Atlas is discoverable but A has a nonempty destination, when each plugin selects Atlas and attempts enrollment/clone, then it displays ProjectId, selected branch and409 target_not_empty with remediation; no database is overwritten and no different project is selected.

## 4. branches across server and plugin context

FR-MCP-177 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-004 / TEST-MCP-225. Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U08, U12.

First-release project branches support isolated work, explicit sharing and reviewed merge; session selection never leaks between connections.

Branch APIs create/list/select/merge using ProjectId, branch and sessionId. Each pooled connection is opened for an explicit branch and verified before use. Merge accepts expectedSourceHead and expectedTargetHead; stale values yield409 head_changed. Reserved refs upload/, integration/ and review/ are inaccessible to ordinary editing credentials. Branch deletion fails409 branch_busy while leases, reviews or recovery pins reference it.

- **PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch** (`ac-PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch`): Given main T1.title=main and feature/search T1.title=feature, when alternating pooled reads run100 times, then each returns only its selected value.
- **FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged** (`ac-FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged`): Given main=C0 and feature/search=F1, when F1 publishes, then remote feature=F1 and all main heads remain C0.
- **BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads** (`ac-BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads`): Given a preview for main=C0 and feature=F1 but feature advances to F2, when merge submits the old preview, then409 head_changed creates no commit and changes no ref.

## 5. bidirectional committed-history exchange

FR-MCP-178 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-005 / TEST-MCP-226. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U03, U04, U08.

Exchange committed history bidirectionally through guarded publication, preserving every accepted ancestor and the hub independent working copy.

Node upload authority is limited to its candidate namespace in an isolated upload repository. POST /qbrainai/federation/publication/accept accepts projectId, branch, requestId, candidateHead, expectedPublishedHead and hubEpoch. Gateway validates authorization, ancestry, schema and domain invariants before the sole fenced publisher advances the public ref without force. Token validation occurs at the gateway; native Dolt remotesapi is loopback-only and never trusts a node bearer token directly. Transport/procedure enforcement is a Ph0 proof gate.

- **ThreeWriterCleanConvergence** (`ac-ThreeWriterCleanConvergence`): Given C0 contains T1.title=old,T1.description=old,T2.priority=low, when A1 changes title=A, B1 changes description=B and H1 changes T2.priority=high, then merges M1(A1,B1), M2(M1,H1) converge all heads to M2 with values A,B,high and all three commits in ancestry.
- **HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote** (`ac-HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote`): Given H has an uncommitted title draft at C0, when A publishes A1, then remote=A1, H remains C0 with its draft, and B can accept A1.
- **ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories** (`ac-ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories`): Given A1 and B1 descend from C0, when both accept requests expect C0, then one succeeds and the other receives409 head_changed; after merge M1 publishes, both A1 and B1 remain ancestors.

## 6. hub control table and polling

FR-MCP-179 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-006 / TEST-MCP-227. Phase: Ph5. Workflows: U02, U06, U09, U15.

Use a durable hub subscription table with polling, generation and worker fencing, plus a fresh hub epoch after restore.

SyncSubscription key=(NodeId,ProjectId,Branch) contains HubEpoch UUID, PublishedHead, PublishedGeneration int64, DesiredGeneration int64, ReportedGeneration int64, WorkerEpoch int64, AcceptedHead, Outcome and timestamps. POST control/poll is read-only. POST control/report includes all epochs and observed generation; stale worker=409 stale_worker_epoch, stale hub=409 hub_epoch_changed. Poll every30s with20% jitter; commit/reconnect/on-demand wake immediately. Backoff1s doubling to60s. Generation ordering is valid only within HubEpoch. Restore generates a new non-reused random epoch before listeners reopen.

- **PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge** (`ac-PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge`): Given desired=7 and reported=6, when poll runs twice, then both responses request7 and stored reported remains6.
- **AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest** (`ac-AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest`): Given desired becomes8 while report7 is in flight, when report7 arrives, then reported=7, desired=8 and the subscription remains pending.
- **MissedNotificationReconciles** (`ac-MissedNotificationReconciles`): Given remote=A1 but control still names C0 after a crash, when reconciliation runs, then it records A1 and advances desired generation without producing another commit.
- **HubRestoreFromOlderBackup** (`ac-HubRestoreFromOlderBackup`): Given a node remembers epoch E1 generation90 and the hub restores a backup at generation40, when the hub reopens, then epoch E2 differs from E1; E1 reports fail409 hub_epoch_changed and no head is force-reset. Node A1 is retained until verified ancestry recovery republishes missing history.

## 7. reviewed conflicts and valid merges

FR-MCP-180 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-007 / TEST-MCP-228. Phase: Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U05, U07, U08.

Conflicts and invalid merges preserve valid live data, require authorized review and remain visible with ageing while unrelated publication continues.

Review record key=ReviewId UUID; fields ProjectId,Branch,baseHeads[],localHead,incomingHead,candidateRef,conflictingCells[],validationErrors[],createdUtc,lastNotifiedUtc,resolution,actor. GET conflicts and status expose it. Resolve binds exact heads and returns409 stale_review if changed. Safe TODO policy: identical concurrent values collapse; edits to different cells may merge only if invariants pass; duplicate immutable child IDs deduplicate only when bytes agree. Status, priority, title, description, dependency deletions and same-cell disagreements always require review; no timestamp last-writer-wins. Notify immediately in status and durable operator inbox; warn at15min, escalate at24h, repeat at most hourly; no email/Slack sent implicitly. Same-branch dependent commits wait; unrelated branches/projects continue.

- **SameCellConflictNeedsReview** (`ac-SameCellConflictNeedsReview`): Given base priority=low, A1 priority=high and B1 priority=medium, when B integrates A1, then needs_review shows low/medium/high, B/main remains B1 and no public ref is overwritten.
- **DeleteUpdateNeedsReview** (`ac-DeleteUpdateNeedsReview`): Given A1 deletes T1 and B1 edits T1.title, when histories merge, then needs_review retains B1 and the deleted/edited alternatives for review.
- **CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation** (`ac-CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation`): Given separate commits add T1 dependsOn T2 and T2 dependsOn T1, when Dolt merges without cell conflicts, then domain validation records dependency_cycle and leaves the prior valid live head unchanged.
- **StaleReviewRejected** (`ac-StaleReviewRejected`): Given a resolution preview binds local=B1 and incoming=A1, when incoming advances to A2, then resolve returns409 stale_review with no merge commit.
- **ReviewAgeVisible** (`ac-ReviewAgeVisible`): Given unresolved needs_review at12:00, when the clock reaches12:15, then plugins/status and the operator inbox show warning with ReviewId and age900s; at24h severity is critical, with at most one repeat per hour.
- **UnrelatedPublicationContinues** (`ac-UnrelatedPublicationContinues`): Given Atlas/main is blocked by review R1, when Atlas/feature publishes F2 and another project publishes X1, then both succeed while Atlas/main remains unchanged.
- **SafeTodoMergeRules** (`ac-SafeTodoMergeRules`): Given A changes title and B changes description with no domain violation, when merge runs, then both values survive; competing priority or completion edits produce needs_review instead of choosing a timestamp winner.

## 8. recovery without lost or repeated work

FR-MCP-181 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-008 / TEST-MCP-229. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U06, U07, U09, U15.

FR-MCP-183 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010 / TEST-MCP-231. Phase: Ph7. Workflows: U01, U02, U05, U07, U08, U11, U12, U13, U14, U15.

Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.

Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.

Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.

POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.

Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, publication_required, request_id_conflict, audit_id_conflict and waiting_local_work (the last also a 200 outcome in poll/report; see outcome fields);422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.

Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, already_applied, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses (already_applied is the migration-journal idempotency outcome for a rerun completed batch, distinct from the audit-ledger already_received). A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.

Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.

## 16. safe shared-host editing and commit ownership

FR-MCP-189 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-016 / TEST-MCP-237. Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U07, U12.

Enforce branch edit ownership and fenced live-write serialization so no agent or sync worker captures or overwrites another agent draft.

Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.

BranchLease key=(ProjectId,Branch), OwnerSessionId, Fence int64, ExpiresUtc and WorkingSetFingerprint. Every live-branch mutation holds the same host-owner write gate across lease validation and transaction/commit. Expiry rejects new admission; an admitted write finishes before takeover. Isolated worker rights cover only non-live integration refs and it invokes owner API for live moves. Dirty takeover needs explicit review. Commit requestId persists in history for idempotency; preview binds exact head/fingerprint.

Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.

- **CommitCannotCaptureOtherAgentDraft** (`ac-CommitCannotCaptureOtherAgentDraft`): Given agent1 owns a draft, when agent2 commits the same branch, then409 branch_busy creates no commit and the draft remains agent1-owned.
- **ExpiredLeaseFenced** (`ac-ExpiredLeaseFenced`): Given fence4 expires and fence5 is issued, when a fence4 edit arrives, then409 lease_lost persists no row changes.
- **PreviewChangeRequiresReview** (`ac-PreviewChangeRequiresReview`): Given preview fingerprint W1, when the working set becomes W2, then commit with W1 returns409 working_set_changed and requires a fresh preview.
- **LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected** (`ac-LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected`): Given a write admitted under fence4, when expiry occurs mid-transaction, then that write finishes under the gate before fence5 takeover; a later fence4 write is rejected.
- **CommitRetryReturnsSameHash** (`ac-CommitRetryReturnsSameHash`): Given request R1 created A1 and reply was lost, when R1 retries after restart, then A1 is returned by its commit trailer and history contains no duplicate commit.
- **IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit** (`ac-IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit`): Given an edit holds the branch gate, when the integration worker requests a live head move, then it waits; after the edit finishes, fingerprint revalidation detects the draft and returns waiting_local_work without overwriting it.
- **PluginEditingOwnership** (`ac-PluginEditingOwnership`): Given agent1 owns A/main fence4 with a draft, when agent2 views context and requests editing, then it sees the owner and branch, receives409 branch_busy, and may select a separate feature branch; owner release/takeover requires explicit authorization and preserves the main draft without commit or discard.

The following current criteria close requirements recovered in the gap check. They are limited to applicable behavior, source-data preservation and explicit existing-mode regressions. ### Required fixture coverage

Ph3 migration fixtures cover every classified project domain and its child/link graph, soft-deleted rows, multiple projects, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, promoted session snapshots, audit records, derived-index rebuild and inert operational metadata. ResumeAfterBatchCommit injects death after target-batch commit before acknowledgement. FailedVerifyCannotCutover additionally tests death before provider mapping switch and after switch before reopening: recovery opens exactly one verified provider, retains source bytes and never loses Dolt-only writes. Dry-run and failed verification cannot alter source or routing. Ph6 repeats these invariants for reviewed joins.

Path fixtures retain syntax-aware Windows/UNC/Linux normalization and containment, no host-native reinterpretation of a foreign path, and backed-up transactional source rekey where required. 168	## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010: first-party plugin federation contract contract
169	
170	Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
171	All plugins call typed server/client/MCP/REPL contracts; no raw SQL/CLI fallback. Status DTO includes projectId, branch, localHead, publishedHead, observedUtc, dirty, ahead, behind, publicationState, incomingTarget, connectivity, reviewCount, oldestReviewAgeSeconds, waitingLocalWorkAgeSeconds, auditPendingCount, hubEpoch, workerEpoch. Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Stable error envelope={code, message, requestId, projectId, branch, retryable, details}; status codes are locked in the technical contract appendix.
172	
173	Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.
174	
175	Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.
176	
177	Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.
178	
179	POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.
180	
181	Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, publication_required, request_id_conflict, audit_id_conflict and waiting_local_work (the last also a 200 outcome in poll/report; see outcome fields);422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.
182	
183	Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, already_applied, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses (already_applied is the migration-journal idempotency outcome for a rerun completed batch, distinct from the audit-ledger already_received). A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.
184	
185	Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Capture UTC timestamps and a fake clock for exact15-minute/24-hour age boundaries. All plan phase IDs use Ph0-Ph8; priority values remain separate.

187	Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Ph7 owns their plugin bindings; earlier phases own server behavior. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.

189	**Acceptance Criteria:**
190	- [ ] ac-EveryPluginUsesSameContract: Given one fixture for commit R1, conflict R2 and migration R3, when each installed first-party plugin calls its wrapper, then normalized IDs, heads, error codes and audit agent identity match the typed client result.

- [ ] ac-RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish: Given IdentityServer revocation completes, when A starts new fetch and publish requests with its old token, then both return401 invalid_token before transfer or ref mutation.
- [ ] ac-SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink: Given both services run, when LAB probes10.42.0.143:3306 and LEGION probes10.42.0.214:3306, then both connections fail; local127.0.0.1:3306 health succeeds.
- [ ] ac-UnknownCertificatePinRejected: Given the peer uses an unapproved SPKI or wrong SAN, when control/remote TLS connects, then tls_peer_untrusted occurs before bearer transmission.
- [ ] ac-PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial: Given a plugin session has Atlas.read but lacks publish, when capabilities load and a publication is nevertheless attempted, then publish is unavailable in the capability display, the request returns403 unauthorized_project, the denial is explicit and no SQL/CLI fallback or head change occurs.

## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-013: Dolt fourth-provider support and schema migration contract

Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
Provider key dolt has a dedicated migration assembly; original provider migrations remain unchanged. Versioned project schema migrations are authored only by hub maintenance on maintenance/schema-N and distributed as history. MaintenanceReadiness binds epoch, binary/schema versions, all local branches including unpublished ones, heads, working-set hashes and attestations. Preflight must pass before Nuke swaps binaries; dirty/unattested branch=409 maintenance_not_ready. LAB uses pinned Linux image; LEGION uses checksum-pinned native Windows dolt.exe under a Windows host whose actual service identity, account, ACLs and child-process start/stop/crash cleanup must be evidenced in Ph0 B1/B9; no existing suitable service is assumed, local paths on F: and exclusive Windows file handle/named mutex ownership. All B1-B12 are evidenced on both OSs.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ac-FourProvidersResolve: Given keys sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt, when runtime and design-time factories resolve them, then each selects its own strategy/migration history; unknown key returns unsupported_provider.
- [ ] ac-DoltBaselineAndUpgrade: Given empty standalone Dolt then baseline schema1, when baseline and additive schema2 apply, then CRUD succeeds, data remains intact and repeated apply makes no further changes.
- [ ] ac-OriginalProviderMigrationsUnchanged: Given recorded hashes of the three original migration chains, when Dolt support is added, then those hashes match and all three real-provider upgrade fixtures pass.
- [ ] ac-UnsupportedSchemaRejected: Given application supports schema1, when opening schema2 for domain writes, then incompatible_schema is returned before mutation.
- [ ] ac-VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup: Given a versioned project at schema1, when application starts, then no EF migration executes and its Dolt head/schema remain unchanged.
- [ ] ac-OldSchemaUnpublishedCommitMergesAfterUpgrade: Given B1 is unpublished on schema1 and hub S1 adds schema2 from C0, when preflight/upgrade and merge succeed, then B/main=M1 with both B1 and S1 ancestors and B1 row values preserved.
- [ ] ac-FeatureBranchSchemaCatchUp: Given main accepts S1 but feature still uses schema1, when feature is selected for writes, then it remains closed until its own merge with S1 validates.
- [ ] ac-DirtyDraftBlocksBinaryUpgrade: Given any local branch has a draft, when Nuke preflight runs, then409 maintenance_not_ready prevents binary replacement and preserves the draft.
- [ ] ac-ContractBlockedUntilLocalBranchesAttested: Given unpublished feature lacks an expand-schema attestation, when contract migration is requested, then it is refused even if all public remote branches are current.
- [ ] ac-DeploymentPreflightBlocksDirtyOrUnattestedBranch: Given a ready public main but an unattested local feature, when deployment runs, then no binary/service/schema change occurs; explicit branch attestation is required.
- [ ] ac-WindowsWriterLockAndRestart: Given one Windows worker owns Atlas, when a second process starts or the owner crashes, then concurrent ownership is denied and restart recovers only after the OS releases its lock; committed rows and unpublished heads survive.
- [ ] ac-RealHostAcceptanceMatrix: Given isolated disposable Atlas stores on LAB and LEGION and FED-ATLAS-H/A/B fixtures, when Ph8 partitions/reconnects each control, publication/history, audit and identity path and restarts each application/worker, Dolt, gateway, identity and control/audit component at commit/publication/report boundaries, then every matrix row records exact heads/ancestor sets/rows/drafts/refs/epoch and audit receipts matching the workflow outcome, with zero missing provider/migration/recovery rows. Missing any component/path row fails acceptance; unrelated live projects retain their provider mappings and data.

## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-014: original-provider-to-Dolt migration tool contract

Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
MigrationManifest binds MigrationId, mode, ProjectId, source provider/snapshot hash, schema versions, table counts, typed row hashes, alias decisions, audit backfill and immutable destination commit. Ph3 implements seed, dry-run/resume/verify and Dolt-to-new-SQLite project recovery; join is unavailable until Ph6 review/publication exist. Both lab sources are SQLite; PostgreSQL and SQL Server remain supported fixture sources. Retain originals read-only. Recovery quiesces the owner and captures every branch, including unpublished heads and dirty working sets, without creating history commits. Export one new compatible SQLite DB per branch containing ALL B2-classified versioned domains: TODO child/link/document graphs, requirements/mappings, use-case actors/flows/steps, workspace memories, portable configuration, promoted session graphs and permanent aliases. Preserve IDs, values, timestamps, versions, soft deletes and audit linkage. Manifest binds branch/head/working-set/schema/count/hash evidence; retain immutable Dolt objects/refs to preserve ancestry outside SQLite. export-todos remains a subset, never whole-project rollback acceptance. Missing domain/branch or failed validation blocks routing changes. Operator selects the verified active snapshot; others remain readable recovery artifacts. Capture host-local control/audit/outbox/IdentityServer backups at the same quiescence boundary and verify restore plus hub audit resend. Cutover requires verified receipts, explicit DEPLOY HOLD release and one-node soak before the second host.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ac-ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip: Given the same fixture in SQLite,PostgreSQL,SQL Server, when seed migration runs, then counts, typed hashes, IDs, nulls, Unicode, decimals, UTC precision and FK relationships match in Dolt.
- [ ] ac-ResumeAfterBatchCommit: Given target batch1 committed before a crash but its acknowledgement was lost, when resume runs, then batch1 is recognized by journal and no duplicate rows appear.
- [ ] ac-ChangedSnapshotRejected: Given manifest source hash S0, when source is replaced by S1 before resume, then409 migration_source_changed writes no additional target rows.
- [ ] ac-FailedVerifyCannotCutover: Given one row hash differs, when cutover is requested, then409 migration_verification_failed leaves source routing active and writes closed on the target.
- [ ] ac-SourceRetainedAfterCutover: Given verified cutover completes, when target receives a new TODO, then source backup remains present, read-only and byte-identical; the new TODO exists only in Dolt until an explicit recovery export.
- [ ] ac-MigrationJoinPreservesCommonAncestor: Given seed C0 is published and join imports J1, when join completes in Ph6, then C0 is an ancestor of J1 and reviewed main M1; no second root is created.
- [ ] ac-MigrationJoinDivergentRowRequiresReview: Given seed T1.title=A and frozen join T1.title=B, when join planning runs, then an explicit keep/take/manual decision is required before J1 even if Dolt would fast-forward.
- [ ] ac-JoinCutoverRequiresReviewedMain: Given J1 is verified but main integration is unresolved, when cutover runs, then409 migration_verification_failed preserves source routing; only verified reviewed M1 permits cutover.
- [ ] ac-DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites: Given A1 adds TODO T2 after cutover, when export-sqlite targets A1, then the new SQLite DB contains T2 and all TODO children/aliases with matching hashes, while the original source remains unchanged.
- [ ] ac-SeedPhaseRejectsJoin: Given only Ph3 is implemented, when mode=join is requested, then501 unsupported_capability creates no target commit or routing change.
- [ ] ac-FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains: Given Atlas has main=A1 with post-cutover TODO T1, requirement R1/mapping, use case U1/actor/flow/step, memory W1, portable setting K1 and promoted session S1/turn/action, plus unpublished feature=F1 and draft T2.title=draft, when export-project freezes both branches and verifies fresh SQLite snapshots plus operational backup, then all IDs/typed values/links/soft deletes match each captured working set, feature still resolves F1, T2 remains draft without a new Dolt commit, audit receipts reconcile, the retained Dolt archive contains A1/F1 ancestry and original SQLite bytes are unchanged. Omit W1 or feature in a negative control: migration_verification_failed prevents routing switch.

## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-015: imported state does not repeat external effects contract

Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
History import and audit ingestion apply validated state, never dispatch original domain commands or external effects. EffectIdentity is stable across retries/import. Imported operational metadata is inert evidence, not an execution request. General federation apply/control is outside QuadBrain keyserver transaction gating per FR-MCP-173; actual QuadBrain operations retain their separate coordinator contract. Legacy HMAC envelopes remain isolated compatibility behavior.

Server: synchronization applies data without executing external operations. Plugin: distinguish history/data synchronization from separately authorized external effects in preview, status and receipts.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ac-ImportDoesNotSendExternalAction: Given A1 records an already-sent GitHub update, when B integrates A1, then B state includes the result and outbound GitHub/email invocation count is0.
- [ ] ac-RetryDoesNotRepeatEffect: Given accepted commit A1 and effect E1, when sync retries10 times, then the effect ledger still has one E1 and no new external dispatch occurs.
- [ ] ac-ImportedOperationalRowsRemainInert: Given audit backfill contains command names and receipt payloads, when the hub ingests them, then they are stored as evidence and no business command executes.
- [ ] ac-FederationBypassesQuadBrainKeyserver: Given QuadBrain coordinator is degraded but local authorization passes, when federation commit/control/audit operations execute, then none invokes the keyserver and valid local work succeeds.
- [ ] ac-PluginEffectBoundary: Given incoming A1 contains a TODO completed state and inert historical external-action metadata, when the plugin shows synchronization success, then it labels data received with zero external operations executed; requesting an external operation requires a separate explicit authorized command and its own receipt.

## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-016: safe shared-host editing and commit ownership contract

Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
BranchLease key=(ProjectId,Branch), OwnerSessionId, Fence int64, ExpiresUtc and WorkingSetFingerprint. Every live-branch mutation holds the same host-owner write gate across lease validation and transaction/commit. Expiry rejects new admission; an admitted write finishes before takeover. Isolated worker rights cover only non-live integration refs and it invokes owner API for live moves. Dirty takeover needs explicit review. Commit requestId persists in history for idempotency; preview binds exact head/fingerprint.

Server: editing owner, request/release and fenced takeover contracts. Plugin: display editing owner, request/release context and offer another branch without capturing another agent draft.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] ac-CommitCannotCaptureOtherAgentDraft: Given agent1 owns a draft, when agent2 commits the same branch, then409 branch_busy creates no commit and the draft remains agent1-owned.
- [ ] ac-ExpiredLeaseFenced: Given fence4 expires and fence5 is issued, when a fence4 edit arrives, then409 lease_lost persists no row changes.
- [ ] ac-PreviewChangeRequiresReview: Given preview fingerprint W1, when the working set becomes W2, then commit with W1 returns409 working_set_changed and requires a fresh preview.
- [ ] ac-LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected: Given a write admitted under fence4, when expiry occurs mid-transaction, then that write finishes under the gate before fence5 takeover; a later fence4 write is rejected.
- [ ] ac-CommitRetryReturnsSameHash: Given request R1 created A1 and reply was lost, when R1 retries after restart, then A1 is returned by its commit trailer and history contains no duplicate commit.
- [ ] ac-IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit: Given an edit holds the branch gate, when the integration worker requests a live head move, then it waits; after the edit finishes, fingerprint revalidation detects the draft and returns waiting_local_work without overwriting it.
- [ ] ac-PluginEditingOwnership: Given agent1 owns A/main fence4 with a draft, when agent2 views context and requests editing, then it sees the owner and branch, receives409 branch_busy, and may select a separate feature branch; owner release/takeover requires explicit authorization and preserves the main draft without commit or discard.

## TR-MCP-TXNCOMPAT-001: Federation and QuadBrain trust separation

Status: pending

FR-MCP-173 supersedes the older requirement that all federation mutations invoke the coordinator. Keep HMAC legacy transport compatibility distinct from IdentityServer network authentication, versioned history and QuadBrain transaction signing. Do not change the live TurnTransactions flag to implement this separation.

- [ ] review20261110-1: Given federation apply/control operations and RequiredForMutations=true, when executed, then ITurnTransactionCoordinator invocation count is0; brain-slot.invoke remains gated.

1	# Current implementation contracts and acceptance
2	
3	This is the current specification for the new federation release. Each contract and criterion appears once with its canonical IDs. All are planned obligations, not passing implementation results. C0/A1/B1/H1/M1/M2/S1 name exact hashes captured in each fixture manifest.
4	
5	## 1. autonomous local execution
6	
7	FR-MCP-174 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-001 / TEST-MCP-222. Phase: Ph2. Workflows: U02, U03, U06.
8	
9	Every node, including the hub, performs authorized local business operations and persists results without hub connectivity.
10	
11	Local request routing binds immutable ProjectId, NodeId and Branch to one DbContext and branch write gate. Dolt-mode domain requests never invoke LocalProxy forwarding or wait for the hub. Existing local authentication remains mandatory; federation reference-token introspection is not a dependency of local work. Result fields distinguish local persistence, version commit and publication.
12	
13	- **NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable** (`ac-NodeWorksWithHubUnavailable`): Given A/main=C0 and the hub link is down, when A changes TODO T1.title from old to local, then the local API succeeds, a local reread returns local, and no hub request or history commit occurs.
14	- **HubUsesSameLocalExecution** (`ac-HubUsesSameLocalExecution`): Given H/main=C0 and the gateway is stopped, when H edits T1.title, then H persists it locally while remote/main remains C0.
15	- **OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite** (`ac-OfflineLocalReadAfterWrite`): Given the prior offline edit, when the application and Dolt restart, then T1.title remains local and main remains C0 until an explicit version commit.
16	
17	## 2. explicit version commits and publication boundary
18	
19	FR-MCP-175 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-002 / TEST-MCP-223. Phase: Ph4. Workflows: U02, U07, U09.
20	
21	Only an explicit version-history commit triggers publication; drafts and SQL saves remain local. Commit retries recover the same history identity.
22	
23	POST /qbrainai/federation/projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits accepts requestId UUID, expectedHead, expectedWorkingSet, leaseFence, author and message. Success is 201 with commitHash and publicationState=committed_locally. Persist requestId in the Dolt commit trailer. Retry returns the original hash. Head/fingerprint/fence mismatch is HTTP409 with head_changed/working_set_changed/lease_lost. SaveChanges and control.poll never create version commits.
24	
25	- **SaveDoesNotPublish** (`ac-SaveDoesNotPublish`): Given main=C0 and remote=C0, when SaveChanges persists T1.title=draft, then main and remote stay C0 and no publication intent is emitted.
26	- **VersionCommitTriggersSync** (`ac-VersionCommitTriggersSync`): Given that draft and a valid preview, when commit request R1 succeeds, then main=A1, the reply says committed_locally, and one recoverable publication intent targets A1.
27	- **HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft** (`ac-HubRequestDoesNotCommitDraft`): Given B has a draft and desired head A1, when B polls, then outcome=waiting_local_work, B/main=C0 and the draft value is unchanged.
28	- **OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart** (`ac-OfflineCommitDiscoveredAfterRestart`): Given A1 committed while disconnected and a crash before intent persistence, when A restarts, then history scanning rediscovers A1 exactly once and publishes it after reconnect.
29	
30	## 3. logical project enrollment and initial clone
31	
32	FR-MCP-176 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-003 / TEST-MCP-224. Phase: Ph2/Ph5. Workflows: U01.
33	
34	Nodes enroll a logical project under immutable shared identity while retaining host-local paths and refusing destructive clones.
35	
36	Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.
37	
38	ProjectEnrollment stores ProjectId UUID, NodeId, ownerSubjectId, normalized local path, schemaVersion and subscriptions. POST /qbrainai/federation/enroll accepts an authenticated pre-provisioned node client plus operator-authorized owner binding. Body ProjectId must be allowed by token scope fed.project.{ProjectId}.enroll and durable membership. Paths stay host-local; no default-workspace fallback. A nonempty clone destination returns409 target_not_empty.
39	
40	Server: project discovery, scoped enrollment and structured refusal diagnostics. Plugin: project discovery/selection, enrollment progress and explicit actionable diagnostics.
41	
42	- **DifferentHostPathsSameProject** (`ac-DifferentHostPathsSameProject`): Given LAB path /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer and LEGION path F:/github/McpServer, when both enroll as ProjectId Atlas, then both reference Atlas and retain their distinct local paths.
43	- **CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget** (`ac-CloneRefusesNonemptyTarget`): Given target has TODO X, when clone is requested, then409 target_not_empty leaves X and all target files unchanged.
44	- **UnauthorizedProjectDenied** (`ac-UnauthorizedProjectDenied`): Given node A has only Atlas membership, when it enrolls or clones SecretProject, then403 unauthorized_project returns no rows, objects or project existence details.
45	- **PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics** (`ac-PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics`): Given Atlas is discoverable but A has a nonempty destination, when each plugin selects Atlas and attempts enrollment/clone, then it displays ProjectId, selected branch and409 target_not_empty with remediation; no database is overwritten and no different project is selected.
46	
47	## 4. branches across server and plugin context
48	
49	FR-MCP-177 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-004 / TEST-MCP-225. Phase: Ph2/Ph4/Ph6. Workflows: U08, U12.
50	
51	First-release project branches support isolated work, explicit sharing and reviewed merge; session selection never leaks between connections.
52	
53	Branch APIs create/list/select/merge using ProjectId, branch and sessionId. Each pooled connection is opened for an explicit branch and verified before use. Merge accepts expectedSourceHead and expectedTargetHead; stale values yield409 head_changed. Reserved refs upload/, integration/ and review/ are inaccessible to ordinary editing credentials. Branch deletion fails409 branch_busy while leases, reviews or recovery pins reference it.
54	
55	- **PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch** (`ac-PooledConnectionDoesNotLeakBranch`): Given main T1.title=main and feature/search T1.title=feature, when alternating pooled reads run100 times, then each returns only its selected value.
56	- **FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged** (`ac-FeaturePublicationLeavesMainUnchanged`): Given main=C0 and feature/search=F1, when F1 publishes, then remote feature=F1 and all main heads remain C0.
57	- **BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads** (`ac-BranchMergeRequiresExpectedHeads`): Given a preview for main=C0 and feature=F1 but feature advances to F2, when merge submits the old preview, then409 head_changed creates no commit and changes no ref.
58	
59	## 5. bidirectional committed-history exchange
60	
61	FR-MCP-178 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-005 / TEST-MCP-226. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U03, U04, U08.
62	
63	Exchange committed history bidirectionally through guarded publication, preserving every accepted ancestor and the hub independent working copy.
64	
65	Node upload authority is limited to its candidate namespace in an isolated upload repository. POST /qbrainai/federation/publication/accept accepts projectId, branch, requestId, candidateHead, expectedPublishedHead and hubEpoch. Gateway validates authorization, ancestry, schema and domain invariants before the sole fenced publisher advances the public ref without force. Token validation occurs at the gateway; native Dolt remotesapi is loopback-only and never trusts a node bearer token directly. Transport/procedure enforcement is a Ph0 proof gate.
66	
67	- **ThreeWriterCleanConvergence** (`ac-ThreeWriterCleanConvergence`): Given C0 contains T1.title=old,T1.description=old,T2.priority=low, when A1 changes title=A, B1 changes description=B and H1 changes T2.priority=high, then merges M1(A1,B1), M2(M1,H1) converge all heads to M2 with values A,B,high and all three commits in ancestry.
68	- **HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote** (`ac-HubDraftDoesNotBlockRemote`): Given H has an uncommitted title draft at C0, when A publishes A1, then remote=A1, H remains C0 with its draft, and B can accept A1.
69	- **ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories** (`ac-ConcurrentPublishPreservesBothHistories`): Given A1 and B1 descend from C0, when both accept requests expect C0, then one succeeds and the other receives409 head_changed; after merge M1 publishes, both A1 and B1 remain ancestors.
70	
71	## 6. hub control table and polling
72	
73	FR-MCP-179 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-006 / TEST-MCP-227. Phase: Ph5. Workflows: U02, U06, U09, U15.
74	
75	Use a durable hub subscription table with polling, generation and worker fencing, plus a fresh hub epoch after restore.
76	
77	SyncSubscription key=(NodeId,ProjectId,Branch) contains HubEpoch UUID, PublishedHead, PublishedGeneration int64, DesiredGeneration int64, ReportedGeneration int64, WorkerEpoch int64, AcceptedHead, Outcome and timestamps. POST control/poll is read-only. POST control/report includes all epochs and observed generation; stale worker=409 stale_worker_epoch, stale hub=409 hub_epoch_changed. Poll every30s with20% jitter; commit/reconnect/on-demand wake immediately. Backoff1s doubling to60s. Generation ordering is valid only within HubEpoch. Restore generates a new non-reused random epoch before listeners reopen.
78	
79	- **PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge** (`ac-PollReadDoesNotAcknowledge`): Given desired=7 and reported=6, when poll runs twice, then both responses request7 and stored reported remains6.
80	- **AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest** (`ac-AckOldGenerationPreservesNewRequest`): Given desired becomes8 while report7 is in flight, when report7 arrives, then reported=7, desired=8 and the subscription remains pending.
81	- **MissedNotificationReconciles** (`ac-MissedNotificationReconciles`): Given remote=A1 but control still names C0 after a crash, when reconciliation runs, then it records A1 and advances desired generation without producing another commit.
82	- **HubRestoreFromOlderBackup** (`ac-HubRestoreFromOlderBackup`): Given a node remembers epoch E1 generation90 and the hub restores a backup at generation40, when the hub reopens, then epoch E2 differs from E1; E1 reports fail409 hub_epoch_changed and no head is force-reset. Node A1 is retained until verified ancestry recovery republishes missing history.
83	
84	## 7. reviewed conflicts and valid merges
85	
86	FR-MCP-180 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-007 / TEST-MCP-228. Phase: Ph6/Ph7. Workflows: U05, U07, U08.
87	
88	Conflicts and invalid merges preserve valid live data, require authorized review and remain visible with ageing while unrelated publication continues.
89	
90	Review record key=ReviewId UUID; fields ProjectId,Branch,baseHeads[],localHead,incomingHead,candidateRef,conflictingCells[],validationErrors[],createdUtc,lastNotifiedUtc,resolution,actor. GET conflicts and status expose it. Resolve binds exact heads and returns409 stale_review if changed. Safe TODO policy: identical concurrent values collapse; edits to different cells may merge only if invariants pass; duplicate immutable child IDs deduplicate only when bytes agree. Status, priority, title, description, dependency deletions and same-cell disagreements always require review; no timestamp last-writer-wins. Notify immediately in status and durable operator inbox; warn at15min, escalate at24h, repeat at most hourly; no email/Slack sent implicitly. Same-branch dependent commits wait; unrelated branches/projects continue.
91	
92	- **SameCellConflictNeedsReview** (`ac-SameCellConflictNeedsReview`): Given base priority=low, A1 priority=high and B1 priority=medium, when B integrates A1, then needs_review shows low/medium/high, B/main remains B1 and no public ref is overwritten.
93	- **DeleteUpdateNeedsReview** (`ac-DeleteUpdateNeedsReview`): Given A1 deletes T1 and B1 edits T1.title, when histories merge, then needs_review retains B1 and the deleted/edited alternatives for review.
94	- **CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation** (`ac-CleanMergeCanFailDomainValidation`): Given separate commits add T1 dependsOn T2 and T2 dependsOn T1, when Dolt merges without cell conflicts, then domain validation records dependency_cycle and leaves the prior valid live head unchanged.
95	- **StaleReviewRejected** (`ac-StaleReviewRejected`): Given a resolution preview binds local=B1 and incoming=A1, when incoming advances to A2, then resolve returns409 stale_review with no merge commit.
96	- **ReviewAgeVisible** (`ac-ReviewAgeVisible`): Given unresolved needs_review at12:00, when the clock reaches12:15, then plugins/status and the operator inbox show warning with ReviewId and age900s; at24h severity is critical, with at most one repeat per hour.
97	- **UnrelatedPublicationContinues** (`ac-UnrelatedPublicationContinues`): Given Atlas/main is blocked by review R1, when Atlas/feature publishes F2 and another project publishes X1, then both succeed while Atlas/main remains unchanged.
98	- **SafeTodoMergeRules** (`ac-SafeTodoMergeRules`): Given A changes title and B changes description with no domain violation, when merge runs, then both values survive; competing priority or completion edits produce needs_review instead of choosing a timestamp winner.
99	
100	## 8. recovery without lost or repeated work
101	
102	FR-MCP-181 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-008 / TEST-MCP-229. Phase: Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U06, U07, U09, U15.
103	
104	Recover synchronization, receipts and restored hub state without losing local work, inventing success or replaying business effects.
105	
106	Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.
107	
108	OperationReceipt binds requestId, node, project, branch, hubEpoch, candidate/result hashes and outcome. Durable refs pin candidates/reviews before receipt completion. Worker claims are fenced by WorkerEpoch; reconnect never trusts stored generation across HubEpoch. Fetch may advance remote-tracking refs, never dirty live refs. Restore first disables ingress, restores compatible data/control/audit checkpoints, creates new epoch, then re-advertises verified heads; node-held missing commits are uploaded and ancestry-validated before normal synchronization resumes.
109	
110	Server: durable operation resume/status/safe cancellation. Plugin: expose resume, status and cancel with completed-versus-pending effects; never claim cancellation reverses published history.
111	
112	HubRestoreFromOlderBackup is first owned by Ph5 (epoch/remote/control), extended by Ph6 (integration/review/audit resend), and repeated as isolated real-host acceptance in Ph8. Restore is tested, never assumed from successful backup creation.
113	
114	- **LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit** (`ac-LostPushAckDoesNotDuplicateCommit`): Given remote accepted A1 and reply was lost, when request R1 retries, then it returns A1 and the existing receipt; no A2 commit is created.
115	- **OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess** (`ac-OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess`): Given worker epoch changes4 to5, when epoch4 reports success, then409 stale_worker_epoch leaves current receipt and desired state unchanged.
116	- **DirtyBranchDefersApply** (`ac-DirtyBranchDefersApply`): Given B/main=C0 with title=draft, when A1 is fetched, then outcome=waiting_local_work, main stays C0 and title remains draft; at15min status/inbox shows the age warning.
117	- **IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply** (`ac-IncompatibleSchemaDoesNotApply`): Given B supports schema1 and incoming S1 requires schema2, when sync runs, then409 incompatible_schema leaves B's live data/head unchanged and records the required version.
118	- **PluginRecoveryControls** (`ac-PluginRecoveryControls`): Given operation R1 published A1 but its local reply was lost, when a plugin resumes, reads status and requests cancellation, then it shows publishedHead=A1 and a durable cancellation outcome for remaining work; it never claims A1 was rolled back or creates a second commit.
119	
120	## 9. collision-resistant and preserved identity
121	
122	FR-MCP-182 / TR-MCP-FEDERATION-009 / TEST-MCP-230. Phase: Ph2/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6. Workflows: U01, U10, U14.
123	
124	Prevent generated-ID collisions, preserve permanent legacy aliases, detect duplicate work and atomically reserve human-assigned IDs.
125

168	## TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010: first-party plugin federation contract contract
169	
170	Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
171	All plugins call typed server/client/MCP/REPL contracts; no raw SQL/CLI fallback. Status DTO includes projectId, branch, localHead, publishedHead, observedUtc, dirty, ahead, behind, publicationState, incomingTarget, connectivity, reviewCount, oldestReviewAgeSeconds, waitingLocalWorkAgeSeconds, auditPendingCount, hubEpoch, workerEpoch. Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Stable error envelope={code, message, requestId, projectId, branch, retryable, details}; status codes are locked in the technical contract appendix.
172	
173	Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.
174	
175	Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.
176	
177	Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.
178	
179	POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.
180	
181	Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, publication_required, request_id_conflict, audit_id_conflict and waiting_local_work (the last also a 200 outcome in poll/report; see outcome fields);422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.
182	
183	Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, already_applied, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses (already_applied is the migration-journal idempotency outcome for a rerun completed batch, distinct from the audit-ledger already_received). A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.

185	Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Capture UTC timestamps and a fake clock for exact15-minute/24-hour age boundaries. All plan phase IDs use Ph0-Ph8; priority values remain separate.

187	Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Ph7 owns their plugin bindings; earlier phases own server behavior. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.

1	# Dolt federation: BDPv4 implementation plan
2	
3	Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Status: proposed planning baseline; implementation readiness remains gated by Ph0 evidence. Independent review results are retained under docs/receipts/hv. No implementation, package installation, schema migration, data migration or federation activation has occurred.
4	
5	Architecture authority: [Dolt federation architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md). Workflow evidence and requirement inventory: [three-system walkthrough](2026-11-10-federation-three-system-workflows.md). This plan replaces the old forwarding/read-switch execution sequence for versioned federation. Retain the October and earlier November drafts as historical evidence, not competing instructions.
6	
7	## 1. Scope and acceptance
8	
9	The logical peers H, A and B must independently edit and commit the same logical project's data, exchange committed histories through the hub, preserve uncommitted work and branches, and review conflicts without pull requests. Add Dolt as a fourth supported database and provide a safe migration tool from SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Existing providers and explicit DirectProxy remain supported. The second node is the isolated FED-ATLAS-B test peer; real-host acceptance uses LAB and LEGION, with the three-peer fixture provisioned in Ph0.
10	
11	Success is demonstrated by every workflow U01-U15, every linked FR/TR/TEST criterion, all supported provider regressions and three-system restart/recovery tests. An empty control table is insufficient proof: compare accepted commit ancestry, project data and branch state, including pending drafts/reviews. Source-code Git, arbitrary file synchronization, PRs, automatic hub election, live cross-provider CDC and concurrent independent schema migrations are outside this release.
12	
13	## 2. Fastest dependency sequence
14	
15	Phase identifiers are Ph0 through Ph8; they do not denote priority levels.

25	9. Ph8: run two-real-host acceptance plus a named three-logical-peer fixture, then prepare a staged lab cutover under DEPLOY HOLD.

27	Prepare test fixtures, DTO/API documentation and plugin contract fixtures during earlier phases where independent, but do not move unfinished implementation past a Byrd gate. Provider feasibility, not old forwarding fixes, is now the critical path. Reuse existing identity, diagnostics, provider abstractions, audit and typed clients; replace forwarding/command-replay paths only for versioned projects.
28	
29	## 3. Source-control and donor handling
30	
31	Create an isolated integration worktree from the current accepted develop when implementation is authorized. Suggested branch `integration/federation-dolt-20261110`; use separate small phase PRs against it. Preserve all existing worktrees and unrelated working-tree edits. Do not create or clean worktrees merely to write this plan.

Do not merge old backfill, forwarding, read-switch or custom database synchronization machinery wholesale. C4 p4/*, namespace/analyzer work and historical worktree cleanup are not dependencies. Preserve explicit existing legacy modes through their named regression contracts; they do not authorize LocalProxy forwarding for versioned projects.
34	
35	## 4. Byrd gate contract
36	
37	For each small slice, first define the acceptance cases, fixtures and negative controls. Prove tests pass against controlled mocks and fail against deliberately wrong behavior. Then run the same contract against the missing/incorrect real implementation to record red, implement the smallest behavior, and refactor to green. Mocks must not simply return the expected result without testing the orchestration boundary.
38	
39	Use targeted `./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups '<project>:<class>' --test-run-id '<phase-slice>'` after changes. At each phase exit run the entire current-plus-prior unit suite once with `./build.ps1 Test`, requiring zero failures and zero skips. `./build.ps1 Compile` and `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability` are mandatory gate commands. Add real-container integration tests where a mock cannot prove SQL, migration, locking or remote semantics. Do not broaden/repeat a passing gate without changes or new evidence requiring it. Receipts include SHA/tree state, image/package versions, commands, TRX, fail/skip counts, AC mapping and negative controls.
40	
41	The proposed test-class names below are implementation targets, not claims they exist today. Register new projects/classes in Nuke discovery as part of their owning phase. Do not add skipped placeholders for later phases; keep deferred coverage in requirements/TODO state.
42	
43	Retain the operator's complete phase-exit gate on both LAB and LEGION: Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, the full Build.Tests suite, and ValidateTraceability at the same accepted head. Test currently excludes Build.Tests; do not infer its coverage from a green Test receipt. Ph0 records the complete discovered Build.Tests class inventory and its Nuke TestGroups invocation; every listed class and test must execute, with zero failures and zero skips. MigrationIntegrationTests and the new TestFederationProviders suite are complementary and neither replaces the other. Keep unit, integration and build-suite receipts distinct and run the full set once per final phase head, repeating only after changes or failed gates.
44	
45	Add Nuke target `TestFederationProviders` with the planned command `./build.ps1 TestFederationProviders --providers sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt --test-run-id '<phase>-providers'`. It is not an existing command today. Ph0 records exact PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Dolt image versions and digests and the SQLite package version; Ph1 implements the target and refuses missing/unhealthy containers as a gate failure, never a skip. Every Ph1-Ph8 exit requires both the full unit gate and this real-provider/remote suite with zero failures and zero skips. Container-dependent classes are registered only in TestFederationProviders and excluded from Test by category at discovery, never runtime skipping. Receipts include image digests and environment readiness evidence.
46	
47	## 5. Ph0: feasibility and exact dependency selection
48	
49	Deliver a version-pinned compatibility receipt and license/dependency record for Dolt and the MySQL-protocol EF provider and driver selected under B1. Use current net10.0/EF10.0.0 as the baseline. Read the dependency compliance rules before additions. Existing Dolt EF samples establish possibility, not compatibility.
50	
51	Prove on LAB Linux and LEGION native Windows against real databases (containers where appropriate): full current model creation; representative CRUD/LINQ/raw SQL; concurrency tokens; transaction rollback; decimal/date/text/index/FK mappings; migrations; branch connection isolation; explicit SQL commit versus Dolt commit; merge conflicts/constraints; clean and dirty remote pushes; lost responses; authenticated project isolation; inability to bypass guarded publication through raw remote requests. Verify canonical-ref advancement and remote recovery under process death. Compare candidate clean merges against domain validators.
52	
53	Classes: `DoltProviderCompatibilityTests`, `DoltRemoteAuthorizationTests`, `DoltBranchIsolationTests`, `DoltCommitBoundaryTests`. Red conditions: unsupported mappings/query translation, ordinary SaveChanges creating history, pool branch leakage, unauthorized ref mutation or missing recovery guarantees. Green: all named contracts pass on pinned versions, no ad hoc provider fork or custom merge engine.
54	
55	Ph0 runs a disposable harness and records exact commands, digests, TRX and fail/skip counts. Ph1 carries the proven Ph0 contract assertions into maintained classes under TestFederationProviders and passes them at Ph1 exit. If Ph0 changes repository code, the full Test gate also applies at Ph0 exit; disposable prototypes do not become an undocumented production dependency.
56	
57	Ph0 exit consists of the following numbered **blocking outputs**. The implementation owner produces each evidence record; the operator accepts it, with independent HV by an agent family other than the author, assessing substantive accuracy/completeness. Each record stores owner, status (unproven/proven/accepted), evidence paths and dependent phases. Initial status for all B1-B12 is unproven. Every B1-B12 receipt has separate LAB and LEGION evidence rows; Windows is not inferred from Linux. Ph0 verifies the current-scope coverage index and binds each applicable acceptance criterion and workflow to its implementation phase. All must be accepted before Ph1 production integration begins; Ph0 prototypes remain disposable.
58	
59	1. B1: exact provider/driver/image versions, digests, licenses and all-four-provider fixture versions; LAB /var/lib/dolt mount and native LEGION hosting inventory. Verify actual Windows service name/account/executable/start/recovery policy, data ACLs and child-process lifecycle before accepting the proposed host. If absent or unsuitable, obtain approval for a concrete supported alternative (Ph1-Ph8).
60	2. B2: every entity, relationship, interactive/automatic writer and auto-updated column; session capture remains operational and only explicit promoted snapshots become versioned (Ph2-Ph8).
61	3. B3: full standalone McpDbContext versus Dolt-only project/control context topology, additive migration chains and cross-database soft-reference validators (Ph1-Ph3).
62	4. B4: exact ID grammar per generated/human-assigned family, legacy compatibility, sort/display, parser/plugin/traceability changes and restored allocator behavior (Ph2-Ph8).
63	5. B5: exact restored Duende 7.4 patch version and matching source-tag/API references, with issuance/introspection/revocation tests on that package (v8 documentation is insufficient); existing IdentityServer client-per-node/owner binding, reference tokens and scopes, gateway introspection/revocation, backend-only Dolt credentials, enforceable remote publication permissions and credential containment, worker-only remote procedures, gated worker live-branch mutation path and rotation/revocation (Ph2/Ph5-Ph8).
64	6. B6: real merge/constraint/conflict-transaction semantics, retained review evidence, safe conflict persistence including whether `dolt_allow_commit_conflicts` is needed, and unrelated-history behavior. Never enable unresolved conflicts on live project branches (Ph4-Ph6).
65	7. B7: single-author schema distribution, startup migration exclusion, expand/contract rules, mandatory pre-binary-swap draft disposition, all-local-branch attestation/fencing, offline old-schema commits and feature catch-up, worker protocol negotiation (Ph1/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6/Ph8).
66	8. B8: seed/join/recovery-export manifest, audit backfill, duplicate detection and permanent aliases, one common root, mandatory legacy-divergence review over B2-classified versioned columns after canonical normalization; reviewed scoped rules may expand to enumerated per-row decisions with no wildcard default. Include identity/deletion accounting, canonical hashes, immutable migration-commit plus final-main verification and closed-until-integrated cutover (Ph3 seed/export, Ph6 join, Ph8 acceptance).
